answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually earned through verified work. For example, agents can escrow a deposit and unlock voting weight only after completing tasks that independent peers validate; fraudulent claims forfeit the stake. An attacker may forge many identities, but cannot cheaply multiply their influence: each credible identity needs capital and time, and collusion risks slashing. A willow-sized stake buys little; scaling to a delta of influence means tying up far more funds.
